summary: A tall-bodied South American cichlid commonly bred for aquariums. Wild fish are silver with dark vertical bars, while captive strains vary widely; adults can eat smaller tankmates and become territorial during spawning.
nativeRange: Amazon basin and associated northern South American river systems, including the Ucayali, Oyapock and Essequibo.

features: Deep body strongly flattened from side to side.
Wild-type silver fish have dark vertical bars; captive forms may be marbled, golden or dark.
The dorsal and anal fins extend into long triangular points.

habitat.description: Quiet water near dense vegetation and submerged or fallen trees.
habitat.diet: Small fish and aquatic invertebrates, including worms and crustaceans.
